items.title: Every UI element is a named asset
items.detail:
Apply the rule across schemas/asset-types.json, the web and Android ports, the 39 starter assets and the conformance fixtures.

- Two tiers: element assets (button, slider, toggle, input, icon, label...) and parent assets (toolbar, menu, nav, app menu, dialog, container, window). A standalone element in a layout is its own named asset; groups only exist inside a parent asset.
- Namespaced ids for every asset (e.g. axf.button.save, axf.toolbar.editor); layouts and parents reference ids.
- Split instance (label, icon, action, state) from skin (style asset + theme tokens).
- Slots with type contracts in layout regions and parents; hot-swap and drag-and-drop = rebinding a slot to a compatible asset id.
- Kernel unchanged (open type registry).

notes.text: Overlaps settings-asset (new `settings` asset type, branch claude/project-thread-55oakl); build with settings-asset-fable.

subPrompts.text: Design note first: write `_claude/memory/docs/named-assets.md` — the two tiers (element assets: button, slider, toggle, input, icon, label; parent assets: toolbar, menu, nav, app-menu, dialog, container, window), the id namespace rule (`<ns>.<type>.<name>`, e.g. `axf.button.save`), instance vs skin split, and which existing starter ids change. List every file the rule touches. No code.

BRETT: review the design note. Decide (a) whether existing starter ids are renamed in place or aliased (old id keeps resolving), (b) whether element assets are required for every control or opt-in per app. Record both answers in the note and in `_claude/memory/decisions.md`.

Schema: in `framework/schemas/asset-types.json` add `"tier": "element" | "parent"` to every type and a top-level `idRule` (regex, documented) for namespaced ids; keep `optional: true` on new fields so old apps validate. Run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs schemas` and `axf validate --framework` — both must pass unchanged.

Validator (web): `framework/core/validate.ts` → `validateAsset` warns (not errors, until the switch flips) when an id does not match `idRule`; add `assetTier(type)`. Add 4 cases to `framework/spec/fixtures/validation.json` (good namespaced id, bare id, element, parent). `npx -y tsx framework/spec/gen-fixtures.mts` then CI check.

Validator (Kotlin + CLI): mirror the id rule in `framework/android/axf-kernel/.../asset/` validator and in the build-engine validator (`framework/cli/build-engine.mjs` validateAsset). Same fixture cases replayed by `ConformanceTest` (written without a compiler: check the "CI build errors" issue after push).

Element asset types, part 1: add `toggle`, `input`, `icon` as `tier: element` types in `asset-types.json` (data shape: label, icon, action, state keys; skin = style-theme tokens only). One starter each under `framework/assets/<type>/`. `axf validate --framework` passes.

Element asset types, part 2: mark the existing `button`, `slider`, `label` as `tier: element`; add the instance/skin split to their spec (`data.instance` {label, icon, action, state} vs `data.skin` {style tokens}) with the old flat shape still accepted by `asEnvelope` normalisation. Fixture cases in `components.json`.

Parent slots: in `asset-types.json` give every parent type (toolbar, app-menu, nav-menu, context-menu, dialog, container, window) a `slots` block like `layout.slots` (named slots + accepted element types), reusing `compileSlots`/`regionAccepts` from `framework/core/engines/layout.ts`. Fixture cases in `layout-slots.json` for one parent.

Rebinding = hot-swap: `framework/core/runtime.ts` gets `bindSlot(parentType, parentId, slot, elementId)` / `unbindSlot` (stored like `attachToHost` in `widgets.ts`, settings key `axf.bind.<parent>.<slot>`); `swap()` of a parent keeps bindings whose types still fit. Unit cases in `widgets.json` → `bindings`.

Kotlin runtime parity: `AxfRuntime.bindSlot/unbindSlot` + KV `<key>:bind` in the kernel, same rules as the TS version, replaying the `bindings` fixture in `ConformanceTest`. Written without a compiler; push and read the CI issue.

Rename the 39 starter assets to namespaced ids (`axf.<type>.<name>`) with the alias map chosen in step 2 (`framework/assets/aliases.json`, read by `registry.ts` + Kotlin `AssetRegistry`): every app manifest and `framework/defaults.json` still resolve. `axf validate --framework` + `validate apps/demo` + console `npm run build` pass.

React layer: `framework/react/components/Controls.tsx` renders an element asset by id (`<AssetButton id>` etc.) reading instance + skin; a standalone element in a layout region renders through the same path. Element Explorer (`react/studio/Inspector.tsx`) shows tier + bindings.

Compose layer: `axf-ui/components/Buttons.kt`, `Slider.kt`, `Controls.kt` take an element asset id the same way; `ElementExplorer.kt` shows tier + bindings. Android console showcase renders one bound element in its toolbar.

Flip the switch: `idRule` violations become errors for apps with `frameworkVersion` ≥ the new one (old apps keep warnings), `axf init` writes namespaced ids, templates updated. Run the CI template sweep locally (`axf init` for react-ts, next-ts, android-compose + validate).

Docs + close: `framework/spec/PORTING.md` section "Named assets"; CLAUDE.md Status bullet; decisions.md entry; mark the pending item complete and the plan feature built; differences report `_claude/memory/docs/rebuilds/named-asset-rule.md` (rule for rebuilds).

items.title: Asset Designer plugin (no-code)
items.detail: No-code editors for nav menus, drawers, app menus, context menus, toolbars, layouts, style packs and color themes. Every asset validates against its schema before save. Adds a drawer asset type. Installed by default.

subPrompts.text: Plugin skeleton: copy `apps/console-web/plugins/_template` to `plugins/asset-designer` (id `ai.amberx.axf.console.asset-designer`, `uiEditor: "builder"`, lifecycle block, `install.mjs`/`uninstall.mjs`), nav → Plugins → Asset designer, Settings → Plugins sub-tab (parent `plugins`). `node framework/cli/plugin-lifecycle.mjs check asset-designer` passes; console tsc + vite build pass.

Designer shell `web/Designer.tsx`: type picker (every non-attachable type from `asset-types.json` the designer covers: nav-menu, drawer, app-menu, context-menu, toolbar, layout, style-theme, color-theme), id + label fields, Save/Cancel; `useEditorSync()` so it reloads values on focus (UI-editor rule). Saves nothing yet.

Validation gate: every save runs `validateAsset` from the baked `src/axf/core/validate.ts`; errors shown inline next to the field they name; Save disabled until clean. Server route `POST /api/plugins/asset-designer/validate` mirrors it with the CLI validator (`framework/core/project-check.mjs` pattern). Test in `test.py`.

Storage: designed assets saved as asset@1 files under `.axf-console/plugins/asset-designer/assets/<type>/<id>.json` (lifecycle dataDir), served by `GET /api/plugins/asset-designer/assets`, registered into the runtime on load like the theme-manager plugin does (`registry.register`, origin `asset-designer`). Built-in ids refused.

Menu editor (nav-menu, app-menu, context-menu): tree of items (label, icon, action, children, divider), drag to reorder, action picker from `rt.actions.list()`, live preview via `rt.swap` on a `ad-preview-<type>` id. Reuses `MenuList.tsx` for the preview.

Toolbar editor: items (icon, label, action, badge counter), `density`/`surface`/`divider`/`collapsible`, widgets start/end picker from `attachable` types (engine-rpc `app-defaults` → `widgets`), live preview through the React `Toolbar`.

`drawer` asset type: add it to `asset-types.json` (hideable chrome, `side` left/right, `width`, `items` like nav-menu, `modal`), `layout.slots` accept it in the `drawer` region, starter `framework/assets/drawer/amberx-side.json`, `framework/defaults.json` names it. Validators on all three ports accept it (Kotlin: `AssetTypeSpec` resource); fixture case in `layout-slots.json`.

Drawer rendering: React `components/Chrome.tsx` draws the drawer region; Compose `axf-ui/components/Chrome.kt` the same (swipe from the edge, scrim from `--fx-opacity-scrim`). Drawer editor in the designer (same editor as nav-menu plus side/width/modal).

Layout editor: region grid (9 regions from `layout.slots`), per-region size/visibility, `data.slots` overrides with accepted-type chips; preview through `compileLayout`. Hidden slots greyed like Appearance does.

Color-theme editor: token groups from the theme engine (`core/engines/theme.ts` token list), colour pickers, contrast warnings (reuse `theme-manager/web/rollEngine.ts` checks), light/dark pair, preview via `rt.swap`.
Style-theme editor: space, radii, borders, font sizes, opacity tokens (`opacityDisabled/Muted/Hover/Tint/Scrim/Glass`), density; preview; numbers clamped to the ranges known themes use.

Templates hook: "Start from" picker listing starters + designed assets + (later) `x.assets.templates` entries; Duplicate / Rename / Export JSON / Import JSON (validated). Export writes a file a user can drop into an app's assets folder.

Installed by default: plugin `enabled: true` in the console's plugin defaults, `framework/catalog/plugins.json` entry (planned → built resolves by itself), `node framework/cli/plugins.mjs --check`, status.json + tracker; Plugin Manager shows it.

Android face (first slice): `axf-devtools` gets an `AssetDesignerModule` placeholder route `asset-designer` listing designed assets received from the console (read-only), so the plugin-inventory shows it on both ports; full editors stay web-only for now (noted as a placeholder capability `axf.designer`).

Tests: plugin `test.py` (validate route, storage, built-in id refused, lifecycle), web unit cases for the drawer slot + layout compile, CI line; `uninstall.mjs --all` leaves nothing (`check --after-uninstall`).

Close: differences report `_claude/memory/docs/rebuilds/asset-designer.md` (new plugin, so a build report), LOG.md line, web screenshots via `rebuild-shots.mjs`, CLAUDE.md Status, plan epic `x.assets.designer` built via `build_step`, pending item complete.

items.title: Asset Browser plugin
items.detail: Browse, preview, import, export and hot-swap assets across apps built on AXF. Installed by default.

subPrompts.text: Plugin skeleton `apps/console-web/plugins/asset-browser` from `_template` (id `ai.amberx.axf.console.asset-browser`, lifecycle, install/uninstall, nav → Plugins → Asset browser, settings sub-tab). Lifecycle check + console build pass.

Sources: server route `GET /api/plugins/asset-browser/sources` lists asset folders it may read: framework starters (`framework/assets`), every app under `apps/*/src/assets` or `app/src/main/assets/axf` (from `framework/cli/app-bundle.mjs list`), designed assets (asset-designer dataDir when present). Never follows symlinks; roots only.
Browse view: grid by type → source → asset, search box (reuses `consoleSearch.ts` provider pattern), type chips from `asset-types.json`, counts per source. Rows show id, label, origin, tier.

Preview: `AssetPreview.tsx` from `framework/react/studio` renders the selected asset in a card; for chrome types a live preview on an `ab-preview-<type>` swap like theme-manager; "Apply here" = `rt.swap(type, id)` after `registry.register`.

Import: drop/paste JSON or pick a file → `validateAsset` → preview → install into a chosen target (console runtime, or an app folder through `POST /api/plugins/asset-browser/install {source, target, type, id}` that writes the file only inside allowed app asset folders; built-in ids refused; backups under the plugin dataDir).

Export: single asset or a pack (zip of asset@1 files + `pack.json`), served by `GET …/export?ids=`; packs are what the plugin runtime (`x.plugins`, PACK kind) will load later, so write the `pack@1` shape now in `framework/schemas/asset-pack.json`.

Hot-swap across apps: for apps running `axf dev` (`framework/cli/dev-server.mjs`), "Push to device" posts the asset to the dev server's folder so the HotReloader picks it up; list dev servers from settings (`axf.devServer`). Error card when none.

Installed by default + Android: enabled in console plugin defaults, `plugins.json` catalog entry, `plugins.mjs --check`; Android `axf-devtools` route `asset-browser` showing the bundled assets by type with Apply (uses `AssetRegistry` + `AxfRuntime.swap`), so Settings → Plugins lists it on both ports.
Tests: `test.py` (sources never leave roots, import validation, built-in refusal, export pack shape), lifecycle check, CI line.
Close: report `_claude/memory/docs/rebuilds/asset-browser.md` + LOG.md + web screenshots, CLAUDE.md Status, plan `x.assets.browser` built, pending complete.

notes.text: Overlaps settings-asset (new `settings` asset type, branch claude/project-thread-55oakl); build with settings-asset-fable.

subPrompts.text: Template index: `framework/assets/templates/index.json` (`asset-templates@1`: id, type, label, tags, file) + loader `listAssetTemplates(type)` in `framework/cli/build-engine.mjs`; engine-rpc `asset-templates`, console `GET /api/asset-templates?type=`. Empty list works end to end.

Validation in CI: `framework/spec/check-asset-templates.mjs` loads every template, runs `validateAsset`, checks unique ids, ≥ 10 per covered type once a type is marked `complete` in the index, and that each type has a `default`. Wire into `android.yml` (node job).

nav-menu ×10: side nav, bottom tabs, rail, grouped sections, icon-only, with badges, two-level, settings-first, admin, minimal. Each a valid `nav-menu` asset in `framework/assets/templates/nav-menu/`.
app-menu ×10 (file/edit/view style menus, single-page apps, tool apps…) + context-menu ×10 (text, list row, card, media, dev, file, link, minimal, with submenus, keyboard hints).
toolbar ×10: editor, media, search-first, compact icons, labelled, split start/end with widgets, status-heavy (counters/progress), collapsible, roomy, minimal.
layout ×10: dashboard, master-detail, sidebar-left/right, bottom-nav phone, kiosk, editor + inspector, chat, settings, full-bleed, three-pane. Each with `data.slots` where it narrows a region.
drawer ×10 (needs `asset-designer` step 7's `drawer` type): left/right, modal/non-modal, wide/narrow, with header, grouped, icon rail, account-first, admin, minimal.

color-theme ×10 light + ×10 dark (pairs): contrast-checked with `theme-manager/web/rollEngine.ts` checks run from a script; names in one family (`arctic-daylight` style). Each pair shares a `pair` tag.
style-theme ×10: glass, flat, outlined, dense, roomy, rounded, square, hairline, soft, print. Numbers inside ranges known themes use; every opacity token present.

Defaults: `framework/defaults.json` + `framework/app-defaults.json` reviewed so every type has a default template id (new field `templates.default.<type>` read by `axf init` for "start from a template"); `axf init --template-set <id>` option registered in `build-options.json` only if it sets a token, else as an init argument.

Run once; commit shots ≤ 60 KB each (`framework/cli/shrink-shots.py`).

Android: templates bundled into `axf-assets` as a resource folder so Compose previews (`ComponentGallery.kt`) and the future Android designer read the same files; `AssetTemplates` Kotlin loader + a unit test that every bundled template validates.

Hooks: asset-designer "Start from" and Build Pilot's designers list templates by type (console `GET /api/asset-templates`); asset-browser shows a Templates source. Add the `templates` capability to `app-defaults` engine-rpc.

items.title: Port engine: bring a non-AXF app onto AmberX AXF (bake or rebuild)
items.detail:
Runs the ports that claude-project parks (pending items port-<name>, manifest x.port, plan in the project at _claude/memory/docs/port-to-axf.md). Brett chose: ask each time between the two ways.

- bake: keep the codebase, run axf init into it (react-ts / next-ts / android-compose), then move its look and chrome into asset@1 assets step by step (colour/style themes, menus, toolbars, nav, dialogs, layout with region slots); UI reads engine tokens only (THEMING.md). Old styles go as each piece moves.
- rebuild: new AXF app from the closest boilerplate (axf boilerplates), old code kept alongside as reference, rebuilt feature by feature on assets/libraries/plugins.

Deliver: axf port <dir> --mode bake|rebuild (analysis report: what maps to which asset types, libraries, plugins; then staged codemods like ui-port.mjs does for UI kits), console + MCP drivers, manifest relation none -> built-on when it starts, fixtures/tests. First real targets: xGallery (MossesX/xGallery, React 19 + Express + SQLite) and whatever claude-project parks.

subPrompts.text: Spec first: `_claude/memory/docs/port-engine.md` — the two modes (bake / rebuild), the analysis report shape (`port-report@1`: stack, UI kit found, screens, chrome pieces → asset types, styles → tokens, libraries/plugins suggested, risk list), the staged codemod plan, and what `axf port` refuses (no manifest, dirty git tree). Read `framework/cli/ui-port.mjs` and `claude-project.mjs` first.

CLI entry: `framework/cli/port.mjs` + `axf port <dir> --mode bake|rebuild [--report-only] [--stage N]` in `axf.mjs`; `requireProject` gate; refuses without `--yes` when git is dirty; writes `port-report.json` next to the manifest. `--report-only` works on an empty folder (empty report).

Stack detection: reuse `claude-project.mjs` detection (react/next/android/python…), add UI-kit detection (MUI, Chakra, shadcn, Material3, Compose, Tailwind) by package.json / gradle deps; unit test with fixture folders under `framework/spec/fixtures/port/`.

Analysis, screens + chrome: scan routes/screens (React Router / Next pages / Compose NavHost) and chrome components (app bar, drawer, bottom nav, menus, toolbars, dialogs) → candidate asset list with target type and confidence. Report section `pieces`.

Analysis, styles → tokens: run `portSource` from `ui-port.mjs` in dry mode over the codebase to count colour/size literals and role usages; map to the token list from the theme engine; report `tokens` with unmapped literals. Cap files scanned (size + count) and skip node_modules/build.

Bake, stage 1: `axf init` into the existing project (template by stack) without overwriting app files (`src/axf/` + assets + manifest relation `built-on`), `axf.lock.json`; app still builds (the template guard allows an existing codebase). Checked with a fixture react app.

Bake, stage 2: themes — generate `color-theme` + `style-theme` assets from the detected palette (nearest tokens), apply the literal → `var(--fx-*)` codemod (`ui-port.mjs portSource`) to CSS/TSX/Kotlin files in place with a `.port-backup/`; `--stage 2` only; report lists every file changed.

Bake, stage 3: chrome — generate nav-menu / app-menu / toolbar / dialog assets from the detected pieces and swap the components for the framework ones (`AppShell` / Compose `AppShell`), old components kept under `legacy/` until removed; `--stage 3`.

Rebuild mode: pick the closest boilerplate (`framework/boilerplates/index.json` tags vs detected features), `axf init --boilerplate` into `<dir>-axf` beside the old code, write `PORT-PLAN.md` with screen-by-screen mapping and the old file for each; report `rebuild.plan`.

Drivers: engine-rpc `port` / `port-report`, console `POST /api/port` + `GET /api/port/report?dir=`, MCP `app_port(dir, mode, stage)` (write, needs the console token); manifest `framework.relation` none → built-on when stage 1 runs (`project.mjs` validates).

Console view: Plugins → **Port** (or Wizards view section): pick a folder from allowed roots (project-wizard's `AXF_WIZARD_ROOTS` rule), run the report, show pieces/tokens tables, run stages one at a time with the file list and a diff count; rebuild plan rendered as a checklist.

Pending items hook: `port-<name>` items (parked by claude-project) get a "Run port" button in Pending rows (slot `pending.item`) that opens the console view on that project; `claude-project` writes `x.port.engine: "axf port"` into the manifest.
First real target, xGallery (MossesX/xGallery, React 19 + Express + SQLite): BRETT attaches the repo; run `--report-only`, review the report together, record the mode choice. No codemod yet.
xGallery bake stage 1–2 on a branch in that repo (init + themes), app builds; note unmapped literals; push branch `axf-port` for Brett to look at on the phone.
Tests: `framework/spec/check-port.mjs` over the fixture folders (detection, report shape, stage 1 idempotent, stage 2 backup + dry run, refusals: no manifest, dirty tree, symlinks); CI line.
Close: report `_claude/memory/docs/rebuilds/app-port-engine.md`, LOG.md, CLAUDE.md Status + `axf port` in Build/run/test, pending complete; decisions.md note on bake vs rebuild defaults.

items.title: lib-clone: any AXF app clones its own install with current data
items.detail:
Turn xGallery's New project wizard (MossesX/xGallery: server/src/routes/newproject.ts, src/pages/dev/newproject/NewProjectWizard.tsx, kit/new-project.mjs) into an AXF library so every app built on AXF can clone its install into a new project. Brett: keep the xGallery wizard as is and make it a library for AXF.

What the xGallery wizard does today (reuse the design): renamed copy from the kit, GitHub repo, per-project deploy key installed on the VPS + Actions secrets (VPS_SSH_KEY, ADMIN_PASSWORD, HOSTINGER_API_TOKEN), Hostinger DNS for site + dev panel, Claude GitHub app access, push main, wait for the site deploy, push panel, wait, first-session prompt; resumable, no secrets stored.

New for the library: clone WITH current data (database snapshot + media/files, consistent copy, secrets and sessions stripped, owner reset), the copy gets its own project.manifest.json + _claude/ (claude-project), cross-port contract (web + Android) for the clone action exposed through the interop gate (default-deny), a settings tab (plugin manager rules: no own settings screen), console + MCP drivers. Open questions for Brett at build time: which data is copied by default, and whether the clone keeps users/members.

notes.text: Oct 18 2026: the project-creation half is built as the console plugin project-wizard (Opus): repo/folder/new AXF app → GitHub/VPS/local homes → manifest, _claude/, Claude.ai project kit, all on claude-project. lib-clone still covers the cross-port library and cloning an install WITH its data; reuse wizard.mjs for the homes and kit.

subPrompts.text: BRETT decides the two open questions before any code: (1) which data a clone copies by default (database snapshot + media? settings? sessions never), (2) whether users/members come along or the clone starts with the owner only. Write both into this item's notes and `_claude/memory/decisions.md`.

Contract `clone@1`: `framework/core/clone.ts` (TS reference) — `CloneRequest` {name, id, homes (github/vps/local like project-wizard), data: {database, media, settings, users}, stripSecrets: true}, `CloneReport`, pure validators (name/id rules from `claude-project.mjs`), exposure descriptor `clone.run` default-deny REMOTE (INTEROP.md). Fixture `spec/fixtures/clone.json` + `gen-fixtures`.

Kotlin mirror `ai.amberx.axf.kernel.clone` (same validators, `ConformanceTest` replay) + Python `framework/python/axf_libs/clone/contract.py` (used by server parts). Placeholder capability `axf.clone` declared in the kernel.

Library scaffold: `axf new-library clone --template service-provider --ports web,android,python` → `framework/libs/clone` (web `AxfWebLibrary` with a settings group "Clone", no own screen), `framework/android/lib-clone`, `framework/python/axf_libs/clone`; `axf compile-library clone` passes. Catalog `libraries.json` entry.

Data snapshot (server, Python): `axf_libs/clone/snapshot.py` — consistent copy of a SQLite db (`sqlite3 .backup`) and listed media folders into a temp dir, strip secret-looking files (reuse project-wizard's patterns), reset owner per the step-1 decision; unit test on a fixture db.

Homes + kit: reuse `apps/console-web/plugins/project-wizard/wizard.mjs` (`run`, `kit`, `link`) for GitHub/VPS/local homes, manifest, `_claude/`, Claude.ai kit; `clone` calls it with `source: folder` after the snapshot is unpacked into the new folder. One code path, no second copy of the wizard.

Web side: `framework/libs/clone/client.ts` (`CloneClient` over the app's API, token via a credential provider like `libs/mcp`), Settings → Clone group (name, id, data toggles from the decision, homes), progress stream (SSE like project-wizard), done screen with links. Gate: `rt.uac` must hold `clone.run`.

Android side: `lib-clone` `CloneModule` → Settings group + `CloneScreen` route `clone` calling the same API through axf-network; `AxfClone` registers the `axf.clone` provider; written without a compiler, CI `:lib-clone:testDebugUnitTest` with a fake server.

Console + MCP drivers: console plugin-free route `POST /api/clone` (admin only) running the Python engine; MCP `app_clone` (write, confirm required = destructive annotation); the console's own Settings → Plugins lists lib-clone like other libraries.

xGallery hook: xGallery keeps its wizard; add a `clone` endpoint there that imports `axf_libs.clone` (or calls the console API) so its New project wizard's "clone with data" uses the library — only after Brett attaches MossesX/xGallery.

Tests + CI: `framework/spec/check-clone.mts` (fixtures, validators), Python `axf_libs/clone/test.py` (snapshot strips secrets, resets owner, refuses symlinks/outside roots), lifecycle not needed (library). CI lines.

items.title: Plugin conflict alarm + tracked AI patches + installed add-ons list
items.detail:
Brett, Oct 18 2026 (parked as unsafe: AI patching and cascading uninstalls need design and review before anyone builds it):

1. When a plugin could potentially conflict with another plugin, raise a developer alarm (alerts library, source conflicts) shown as an expandable row grid like the Systems check grid: same kinds of details per row, fix instructions and external links.
2. Each conflict row has 3 badges/actions: (a) uninstall a plugin - choose which one; (b) ignore; (c) use AI to patch the conflict. The patch must NOT alter any plugin source.
3. Patches are tracked and listed in an Installed add-ons list that covers plugins, add-ons, modules, libraries and patches. Installing a patch is tracked and the patch can be removed.
4. Removing a patch uninstalls every conflicting plugin it patched; those plugins must then be reinstalled.

Builds on: alerts library (conflicts source, diagnostics: same asset id / setting key / settings tab from two named modules; plugins:dup ids on the server), plugin-lifecycle@1 (install/uninstall scripts, backups), plugin-manager (Fable, pending), agent manager add-ons (agent-addon@1 install/uninstall tracking), axf.llm@1 for the AI patch.
Open questions for Brett at build time: what counts as a potential conflict beyond the runtime diagnostics (routes, capability services, settings keys, assets, nav ids, CSS prefixes, data dirs?); where patches live (an overlay layer the console applies at load, never the plugin folder); whether removing a patch should back up the plugins first and offer one-tap reinstall.

notes.text: Oct 22 2026: patches-plugins (Opus) adds Patches-owned plugin lists per hosted app and an auto install of missing plugins; check for overlap when this is designed.

subPrompts.text: Design note, part 1 (no code): `_claude/memory/docs/plugin-conflicts.md` — what counts as a potential conflict beyond runtime diagnostics: routes (`/api/plugins/<f>/`), capability services (two providers of one `axf.x@1`), settings keys, asset ids, nav ids, CSS prefixes (`axp-*`), data dirs, Python module names. For each: how it is detected from `plugin.json` + the bundle + `plugin-inventory@1` facts, severity, false-positive risk.

Design note, part 2: patches. Proposal: a patch is an **overlay** (`.axf-console/patches/<id>/patch.json`, `plugin-patch@1`: target plugins, kind rename-route / remap-setting / alias-asset / disable-contribution, applied by the console at load, never touching a plugin folder); AI only proposes a patch document, a person approves it (change-batch card); removal backs up + offers one-tap reinstall. Risks and what is refused.

BRETT reviews both notes and answers the three open questions (conflict kinds in scope, overlay approach yes/no, backup + reinstall on patch removal). Status stays `unsafe` until he says the design is approved; then `pending`. Record in decisions.md.

Conflict engine (pure): extend `framework/core/engines/plugins.ts` (`plugin-inventory@1`) with `potentialConflicts(records)` for the approved kinds, severity + fix hints; Kotlin `PluginInventoryEngine` + Python `plugin-manager/server/engine.py` mirror it; fixture cases in `spec/fixtures/plugin-inventory.json` → `conflicts` (`check-plugin-inventory.mts`, `test.py`, `PluginInventoryConformanceTest`).

Alerts source `conflicts`: `apps/console-web/server/alerts.py` raises one alert per conflict key (`conflict:<kind>:<a>:<b>`, warn, resolved when it disappears) from the engine output every poll; rule default: bell on. Test in `server/test_alerts.py`.

Conflict grid UI: plugin `apps/console-web/plugins/plugin-conflicts` (from `_template`) with a dialog `plugin-conflicts.grid` built on the Systems check grid component pattern (expandable rows: details, fix instructions, links); opened from the alert's link and from Plugin Manager rows. Read-only this step.

Row actions (a) Uninstall — pick which plugin, confirm by typing its folder, runs `plugin-lifecycle.mjs uninstall --all` through the existing `/api/plugin-lifecycle/<folder>/uninstall`; (b) Ignore — stored per conflict key in the plugin dataDir, hides the row and resolves the alert; both admin-only.

Patch overlay runtime: `server/patches.py` loads `plugin-patch@1` files, validates them against the schema (`framework/schemas/plugin-patch.json`), applies approved kinds at plugin load (route prefix rename, settings key remap, asset alias, contribution disable) in the loader, never writes into plugin folders; `GET /api/plugins/plugin-conflicts/patches`.

(c) AI patch: "Patch with AI" asks Mosses through `axf.llm@1` for a patch document for this conflict (prompt includes the engine facts), validates it, shows it on a change-batch-style approval card; Apply writes the file and reloads plugins; refused when the assistant is off (409 with what is missing).

Installed add-ons list: dialog + Settings → Plugins → Add-ons listing plugins, libraries (`plugin-inventory`), modules, agent add-ons (`agent-addon@1` from `axf.agents@1` when present) and patches, each with installed date, what it touches, Remove. Patches show which plugins they patch.

Patch removal: Remove patch → backup (`.axf-console/plugin-backups/`) → uninstall every plugin it patched (lifecycle) → list them with one-tap Reinstall from the catalog (`plugin-catalog.mjs install`) when the step-3 decision says so. Audit line per action.
Tests: plugin `test.py` (grid data, ignore, patch validation + refusals, removal cascade with fake lifecycle), engine fixtures, lifecycle check, CI lines.
Close: report `_claude/memory/docs/rebuilds/plugin-conflicts.md`, LOG.md, web screenshots, CLAUDE.md Status, rules line about patches never touching plugin folders, pending complete.

items.title: Agents + assistant sessions hosted on axHub (one host for every app)
items.detail:
Brett, Oct 20 2026: agents (Build Pilot's pilot-assembler, Mosses and every agent-definition@1 agent) and AI assistant live sessions should run on axHub, not inside each app. Build Pilot, the Dev Console and the phone apps become clients.

- axHub gets an agent + session host: runs turns, owns live-session@1 event logs (sessions survive app restarts and browser closes), per-agent memory, provider keys in axHub's vault, hub permissions for who may use which agent.
- Apps plug in through what the Fable rebuilds left open: the live-session host registry (`axf.live-host@1` / `register_host`, today a typed `axhub` placeholder in the console and Build Pilot), Build Pilot's assembly backend (BP_AGENT=local|console|off → add `axhub`), and the kernel placeholders `axf.agents`, `axhub.agent`.
- axHub never depends on AXF (decision): the host speaks the contracts over its API (AXPP), with an AXF adapter on the AXF side (lib-hub).
- The assembly gate (pilot-assembly@1) stays in Build Pilot: axHub only proposes ops; Build Pilot checks and builds. Manual mode unaffected.
- Needs the axHub repo (MossesX/axHub) attached.

Until then: Build Pilot runs its agent locally (Fable rebuild Oct 20 2026), the console's assistant hosts its own sessions.

subPrompts.text: BRETT attaches MossesX/axHub. Read its session/worker layout, decisions #70–#87 and the AXPP protocol doc; write `_claude/memory/docs/axhub-agent-host.md` design: host API (sessions, turns, events, agents, memory, permissions), where provider keys live (vault, write-only), what the AXF adapter translates. No code.

Protocol contract (AXF side, pure): `framework/core/live-session.ts` gains the wire shape for a remote host (`RemoteHostDescriptor`, event envelope with seq, resume cursor), fixtures in `spec/fixtures/live-session.json` → `remote`; Kotlin `ai.amberx.axf.kernel.live` + Python mirror replay them.

axHub, session store: `sessions` table/collection (id, owner, agent, created, closed, cursor) + append-only event log keyed by seq (file or db per axHub's storage), with replay from a cursor; unit tests.

axHub, turn runner: a worker that runs one turn for a session (provider call through axHub's existing LLM client or a new one using vault keys), streams events into the log, survives the browser going away; one running turn per session; stop/cancel.

axHub, agents: `agent-definition@1` validator ported from `framework/core/agents.ts` (fixture `agents.json` replayed), agent registry per project in `/projects/<name>/_data/agents/`, per-agent memory using the memory engine rules from the contract.

axHub, permissions: who may use which agent / open sessions / write mode, as hub user permissions (`agents.use.<id>`, `sessions.open`, `agents.write`) on the users page, enforced on every host route; admin bypass as elsewhere on the hub.

axHub, host API: `/agents`, `/sessions`, `/sessions/{id}/turns` (POST = run), `/sessions/{id}/events?since=` (SSE + replay), `/sessions/{id}/stop|close`; approvals for destructive tool calls through the hub's approval screen (one-tap link rule). OpenAPI snippet in the design doc.

axHub, provider keys: turns use keys from the vault by name (`llm.<provider>`), never returned; `vault.set` from the console's Keys needed flow already exists — add the names to the systems-check key list on the AXF side later (step 15).

AXF adapter, web: `framework/libs/hub` (lib-hub, first slice exists) gets `AxhubLiveHost implements SessionHost` over the host API with the hub session cookie / token provider; registers through `axf.live-sessions@1.register_host()`; the console's AI assistant picks it when Settings → Assistant → Host = axHub.

AXF adapter, Android: `lib-hub` Kotlin `AxhubLiveHost` over axf-network (SSE reader from `lib-mcp`'s parser), registered in the kernel's live-session host registry; placeholder `axhub.agent` becomes real; written without a compiler, CI unit test with MockWebServer.

Console assistant on the hub host: `ai-assistant` plugin `server/sessions.py` host `axhub` stops being a `PlaceholderHost`: a thin proxy host that forwards to the hub API with the signed-in user's identity; reconnect/replay through the existing `watchReply` fold; `test.py` cases with a fake hub.

Build Pilot: `BP_AGENT=axhub` backend in `server/assembly.py` calling the hub host for the `pilot-assembler` agent; the assembly gate (`pilot-assembly@1`) still checks every op locally; manual mode untouched; `test_server.py` with a fake hub.
Phone apps: the AXHub Android app gets a Sessions tab (list, attach to a live reply, stop) on `lib-hub`'s host client; the Android console's assistant screen (when it exists) uses the same.

Migration: console sessions stored locally can be exported/imported into the hub (`POST /sessions/import` with the event log); one-time "Move my sessions to axHub" button in the assistant settings; no data loss on failure (import is additive).
Systems check: new checks `axhub-agent-host` (host reachable, caller allowed) and the vault key names for providers in the Keys needed list; Auto fix opens the right pages.
Alerts + activity: hub sessions appear in the Activity banner source list (`axf.activity@1`), failed turns raise an alert via the hub → console alerts source `axhub`.
Tests, AXF side: `check-live-session` fixture cases for the remote shape, lib-hub web unit tests (fake SSE), Android unit test, plugin `test.py` additions; CI lines in `android.yml`.
Tests, axHub side: host API tests (permissions, replay from cursor, one turn per session, stop), agent validator fixture replay, vault key never returned.

Deploy: axHub redeploy on Coolify with the worker enabled (env for worker count), console `install-console.sh` passes `AXF_ASSISTANT_HOST=axhub` once the hub answers; BRETT approves the deploy and runs one turn from his phone.
